structure.heading: Enterprise Data Ownership and Classification Policy (Scope, Accountability, and Handling Controls)
text_content: **Enterprise Data Ownership and Classification Policy (Scope, Accountability, and Handling Controls)**

Effective 2026-07-01, the policy applies enterprise-wide to twelve discrete data domains. 100% of these 12 enterprise data domains must have a named Data Owner and a named Data Steward by 2026-09-30. Scope includes structured, unstructured, master, reference data and associated stakeholders and thirdp-arty custodians.

Accountability is explicit: the Chief Data Officer assigns Data Owners who hold decision rights; Data Stewards manage operational controls. Legal and Security provide compliance oversight. All role assignments require documented signoff and an audit record within 14 days of assignment per enterprise standards.

The classification policy defines four levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. Handling controls vary by class: Public requires open dissemination; Internal requires authenticated access; Confidential requires role-based access, masking, and 100% encryption at rest and transit; Restricted requires multi-factor access, 256-bit encrytpion, and retention controls.

Enforcement includes monthly compliance reporting to the CDO and quarterly audits thereafter; progress toward the 2026-09-30 assignment deadline will be reported weekly until 100% completion. Exceptions are approved by CDO with Legal and capped at 5% of datasets per domain, documented and timebound.

structure.heading: Data Quality, Lineage Requirements, and Governance Operating Model (Roles, Cadence, and Decision Rights)
text_content: **Data Quality, Lineage Requirements, and Governance Operating Model (Roles, Cadence, and Decision Rights)**

Data quality targets for Tier-1 Critical Data Elements (CDEs) are mandated and measurable: each Tier-1 CDE must achieve at least 98.5% completeness and 99.0% accuracy on a rolling 30-day basis. Quality metrics are computed daily and published in the enterprise Data Quality Scorecard; monthly exceptions trigger formal remediation plans. The Data Quality Office maintains SLAs: critical defects require a root-cause analysis within five business days and a documented remediation plan within ten business days. Sampling, automated validation, and reconciliation rules are defined per dataset, and acceptance gates are enforced before downstream consumption.

ELT pipelines, streaming processes, and analytic models to capture transformation logic, timestamps, and version identifiers into the enterprise metadata repository. Exceptions requiring manual annotation will be tracked and limited to documented justifications. Quarterly lineage audits will validate coverage claims and feed into compliance reporting. Integration with the data catalog and impact analysis tools is mandatory to support change management and regulatory traceability requirements.

The governance operating model defines roles, cadence, and decision rights: the Data Governance Council meets on the first Tuesday of each month to adjudicate policy exceptions, approve Tier-1 CDE definitions, and ratify strategy. Data owners retain decision rights for data access and retention, while business data stewards execute daily stewardship tasks and the Data Quality Office enforces measurements. A RACI matrix documents responsibilities across IT, Legal, and Compliance. Regular cadences include weekly stewardship huddles, monthly council reviews, and quarterly executive reporting tied to KPIs and funding decisions.
